premise_falsified.why_wrong: The T21 sweep (Qwen3-32B x variable_tracking x resume_j in {3,6,13,20,27,34,41,48} x {16k,32k}, n=50/cell) does NOT use the same 50 samples across configs. Measured on zwfy6 by md5-ing the full question text and the target column: j3 INTERSECT j6 = 0/50, j3 INTERSECT j13 = 0/50, ... j3 INTERSECT j48 = 0/50. Target column intersections are also 0/50. RULER variable_tracking is synthesised at eval time and the sample identity was never fixed or seeded per config.
premise_falsified.consequence: per-example oracle requires the SAME example measured under different configs, to compute oracle = max_config(quality) and regret = oracle - best_fixed_config. With disjoint sample sets neither quantity is computable. Only cell-level 'best fixed config' can be computed -- which is precisely the baseline the oracle is supposed to beat, not the oracle.

kill_gate.why_it_had_to_be_written: PROPOSAL.md Stage 0 says only 'if the oracle's gain over the best fixed config is insufficient, close the direction'. That is NOT decidable: with C configs and noisy per-item outcomes, oracle - best_fixed is positive by construction even with zero exploitable structure, so 'insufficient' has no non-arbitrary threshold.
kill_gate.verbatim: B02's premise is that the best configuration varies per query, so a query-adaptive controller can beat the best single FIXED configuration. The direction is KILLED unless BOTH clauses pass, each on EACH length independently (no pooling across lengths). CLAUSE 1 (complementarity must clear its own independence floor): on the FRACTIONAL-recall scale, with Delta_excess = oracle_obs - mean(oracle under Null A), where Null A independently permutes each config's outcome column across items (B=10000 draws, seeded PCG64, single node, numpy version recorded), require Delta_excess > 0 AND its 95% permutation interval to EXCLUDE 0. CLAUSE 2 (the headroom must be REACHABLE, not merely present): a router restricted to PRE-ANSWER features (input length, evidence count, retrieval-score statistics) must beat the best fixed configuration OUT-OF-SAMPLE, where the comparator's fixed configuration is ALSO selected on the training half; pass requires the 95% interval of the held-out gain to EXCLUDE 0. Both clauses failing => B02 is killed as a router direction. Pre-committed wording: n=200 resolves |Delta_excess| >= 0.033 at 80% power, so an interval CONTAINING 0 must be written as 'no effect larger than 3.3 pp', never 'no effect'.
why_not_degenerate: The statistic is not a function of the margins the null preserves. Null A preserves COLUMN margins and destroys item-x-config coupling; the oracle mean_i max_j M[i,j] is a function of ROWS. Permuting each column independently changes which values co-occur in a row, so there is no invariance argument. MEASURED Null-A sd on the real confirmatory matrices: 0.01039 (16k frac), 0.00897 (32k frac), vs Null B's 5.55e-17 = floating-point zero.

Moving to the FRACTIONAL scale removes the binary identity that caused the degeneracy at all. The Null-B proof needs max_j to be determined by the row sum, which holds only for {0,1} entries. Counterexample on [0,1] recall with 2 configs: row (0.50,0.00) and row (0.25,0.25) have the SAME row sum 0.50 but oracles 0.50 vs 0.25. So on the fractional scale even a row-margin-preserving null would NOT be invariant -- the gate is robust to the whole CLASS of failure that killed Null B, not just to one instance.

Clause 2 cannot degenerate into a tautology either: the comparator fixed config is re-selected on each training split, so the gate is not 'router beats a comparator tuned on the test set'. This is the selection-validity flaw named by arXiv:2608.08265.
kill_gate.explicitly_NOT_primary: Null B (both-margins / curveball) is RETIRED for any binary per-item oracle and must never again be pre-registered as primary in this repo. PROOF: for binary correctness max_j M[i,j] = 1[rowsum_i >= 1], so the oracle depends on ROW MARGINS ALONE, and curveball preserves row margins exactly => the oracle is EXACTLY invariant under Null B, every draw, by construction (measured sd 2.22e-16, p=1.0). It would return p=1.0 on every dataset forever and be misread as 'the kill clause fired'. GENERALISES: for a binary per-item oracle, item difficulty and oracle value are THE SAME QUANTITY.

clause_1_complementarity.reading: The raw headroom looks large (+21 to +25 pp) and is ENTIRELY BELOW its own independence floor. Configs are POSITIVELY COUPLED: hard items are hard at every depth. clause_2_realizability.result: FAILED -- no pre-answer-feature router beats a train-selected fixed j, at either length
clause_2_realizability.estimator: 300 random 50/50 item splits; per-bucket best j learned on TRAIN and applied to held-out TEST; comparator fixed j ALSO train-selected (selection-valid)
clause_2_realizability.STRUCTURAL_finding_more_decisive_than_th: B02's own input features are DEGENERATE on the task its own sweep uses. (a) 'document length': RULER pads every item to the target length -- measured span is 10 tokens out of 32713-32723, sd=1.96. (b) 'estimated evidence count': CONSTANT at 9 for every item in variable_tracking, so a router keyed on it is IDENTICALLY the best fixed config. PROPOSAL.md lists 7 input features; on this task two are constants and the retrieval-side ones (BM25/dense score gap, retrieval entropy) are not emitted per item by the harness. So Clause 2 could not have been passed on variable_tracking by ANY amount of GPU, and B02's Stage 0 as written was never decidable on this task alone.

kill_gate_verdict.surviving_positive_result: The depth curve's SHAPE and PEAK are stable across context length: Spearman over the 8 j values between 16k and 32k mean recall = +0.976, and j=27 is the best arm at BOTH lengths. Combined with the negative Delta_excess: on this task ONE well-chosen FIXED split depth is the right answer and it transfers across length. Per-query depth adaptation has no complementarity left to exploit.

methodological_carry_forward.finding: For a binary per-item oracle, item difficulty and oracle value are THE SAME QUANTITY: max_j M[i,j] = 1[rowsum_i >= 1], so any row-margin-preserving randomisation (curveball / swap / within-row permutation) leaves the oracle EXACTLY invariant. A both-margins null therefore cannot separate complementarity from difficulty, and pre-registering one as primary guarantees a p=1.0 that will be misread as 'the kill clause fired'.
methodological_carry_forward.novelty_of_the_finding: The curveball/both-margins null is standard in ecology, and 'oracle max is upward biased' is folklore that arXiv:2607.03436 and arXiv:2605.09618 gesture at. The specific statement that the both-margins null is degenerate BY CONSTRUCTION for a binary max-statistic returned 0 hits on four separate query shapes.
methodological_carry_forward.HONEST_SIZING: This is a paragraph, not a paper. Worth a footnote or methods appendix in any write-up reporting per-item oracle headroom, and worth recording so nobody in this project re-pre-registers Null B. NOT grounds for promotion. B02 is NOT promoted.
methodological_carry_forward.binding_rule_for_future_gates: Any future per-item oracle gate in this repo MUST use a column-margin (Null A) primary on a NON-BINARY outcome scale, and MUST include a Clause-2 out-of-sample realizability leg with a TRAIN-SELECTED comparator. Both are encoded in KILL_GATE_VERDICT.md sec 2 and implemented in analyze_b02_oracle.py.

abandoned.original_claim: The optimal configuration varies per query, so a learned controller that jointly selects read method (raw replay / CoMem / reusable KV), split depth j, evidence budget k, retrieval rounds, and a low-confidence fallback will beat any single fixed configuration -- targeting quality within 1pp of the per-example oracle on a held-out task family together with a >=20% reduction in mean Read latency.
abandoned.killed_by: Its own pre-registered kill gate B02-KILL-1, fired on the n=200 confirmatory sweep (VT x {16k,32k}, Qwen3-32B, chat=False, 6.44 GPU-h measured on .73). CLAUSE 1: the per-item oracle sits BELOW its own independence floor at both lengths -- Delta_excess = -0.039 (16k) and -0.032 (32k), both p=0.0008, both 95% intervals excluding 0 on the NEGATIVE side -- i.e. configs are positively coupled (hard items are hard at every depth), which is strictly worse for a router than no signal. CLAUSE 2: no pre-answer-feature router beats a train-selected fixed j out-of-sample at either length, AND two of the seven input features PROPOSAL.md names are literally constant on this task (document length spans 10 tokens out of 32k; evidence count is exactly 9 for every item), so the clause was unpassable on variable_tracking by any amount of GPU. Prior art did NOT kill this -- the novelty gate came back CLEARED (no located work does within-model split-depth oracle headroom).
abandoned.surviving_scope: TWO things survive, both small and both honestly stated. (1) A POSITIVE empirical result about fixed depth: the depth curve's shape and peak are stable across context length (Spearman over the 8 j values, 16k vs 32k = +0.976; j=27 best at both), so ONE well-chosen fixed split depth transfers and per-query depth adaptation is unnecessary on this task -- this is a useful negative-space result for paperA's split-depth story, NOT a paper of its own. (2) A METHODOLOGICAL note: the both-margins (curveball) null is provably degenerate for any binary per-item oracle because max_j M[i,j] = 1[rowsum_i>=1]; worth a footnote wherever per-item oracle headroom is reported, and now a binding rule for future gates in this repo. WHAT DOES NOT SURVIVE: the controller, the +20% latency target, the <=1pp-to-oracle target, and any claim that query-adaptive depth/budget selection has exploitable headroom. Scope limits that must be stated with (1): ONE task (RULER variable_tracking), ONE model (Qwen3-32B), ONE selector (iter_bm25, topk=12), n=200 per arm. n=200 resolves |Delta_excess| >= 0.033 at 80% power, so the negative is 'no exploitable complementarity larger than 3.3 pp on this task', not 'no complementarity anywhere'. A different task with genuinely variable evidence count could still show headroom -- but B02 as scoped is closed, and re-opening it requires a task where the input features are not constants.
